dryDock.orders_meta: Rev 3, 11 Aug · §4 amended in the margin on 12 Aug by Kasai · high water 1.47 m at 19:22
dryDock.orders_ask_label: Inquiry from the pump house · 20:58 · channel 12
dryDock.orders_ask: “The surveyor wants the gate seals. Can I take key 4-B off the board and open the seaward valve for ten minutes?”
dryDock.orders_ask_by: Miura, pump house. He is holding the channel until you answer, and the answer goes in the log either way.
dryDock.orders_lead: The ship is on the blocks and the keel walk is not in the book yet. The typed §4 and the margin of §4 do not say the same thing, so read the margin before you answer. Nothing on this page has been retyped since 11 Aug.
dryDock.orders_affix_label: Answering the pump house, 20:58 · clause in force
dryDock.orders_affix: §4 — the seaward valves stay locked until Ogawa has walked the keel
dryDock.orders_p1: §1 — Watch. Third watch takes the dock from 19:00. Handover is at the pump house, not the office. The log from second watch is two lines: tide rising, no one on the blocks.
dryDock.orders_p2: §2 — PACIFIC HORIZON, inbound for propeller work. Displacement 14,820 t. The blocking plan is rev 3, dated 11 Aug. Block 7 on the port quarter was packed twice; the first pack settled 12 mm.
dryDock.orders_p3: §3 — Lights. Floodlights on the blocks stay on until the keel walk is signed. Crane 2’s cab light is on a separate circuit and goes off with the shed.
dryDock.orders_p4: §4 — Flood. Valves on the seaward culvert stay locked. Keys on the board in the pump house, tag 4-B. Do not open for a “quick look” at the gate seals. The amendment is the sentence Kasai added in the margin: “locks stay on until Ogawa has walked the keel.” He did not rewrite the paragraph. The typed text still says the surveyor “may request a partial flood to inspect the gate.” That sentence is dead. The margin is what is in force.
dryDock.orders_p5: §5 — Radio. Channel 12 for the dock, 16 only if the harbour asks. The office phone is 0143-22-4108. If the pump house does not answer, walk. Do not keep calling.
dryDock.orders_p6: §6 — Crane 2. Hoist is not to move while anyone is under the port quarter. The cab has the list. If the list is not in the cab, the hoist stays down.
dryDock.orders_p7: §7 — Tide. Tonight’s high is 1.47 m at 19:22. The sill is at 0.80 m. If the harbour revises the tide, rewrite this line. Do not leave the old figure.
dryDock.orders_p8: §8 — Pumps. Number 2 dock pump has a leaking gland and is out until the yard fits a new one. That leaves 1 and 3, so a full drain takes six hours now, not four. Work the flood and the drain around that figure, not the one on the board.
dryDock.orders_p9: §9 — Hot work. Welding on the shaft bracket stopped at 17:40. Fire watch on the port quarter runs an hour past the last arc, so it closed at 18:40, but walk the quarter once more before midnight. The extinguisher on the catwalk is out of date and the yard has been told twice.
dryDock.orders_p10: §10 — Gangway and shore power. The gangway is rigged aft and moves with the tide; look at the lashing every time you pass it. Shore power is the quay box, 60 A. If the box trips, the ship loses lighting before the bilge alarm goes, so look for a dark hull first.
dryDock.orders_p11: §11 — Fog. If the crane 2 cab cannot be seen from the pump house, sound the dock signal every two minutes and tell the harbour on 12. It came down at 20:40 tonight and has not lifted.
dryDock.orders_p12: §12 — End of watch. Leave the board as you found it. The flood keys are either on 4-B or in someone’s pocket, and last Tuesday they were in a pocket. Write the name.
